data.title: test(social): assert the registry name-persist mechanism instead of p50 ordering (bn-2cye)
data.description:
bn-2cye. seed_profile_smoke asserted new-stream append p50 > warm append p50 — a strict microsecond ordering with zero margin. It failed under full-suite parallel load on 2026-07-28 (new=18.097us vs warm=19.118us) while passing 3/3 in isolation.

Fix = option (c): assert the countable mechanism, not its performance shadow.

Mechanism chosen: $registry RECORD COUNT (not fsync count).
Why not fsync: the harness (fresh_prof_backend) opens LogEngine with default options = Durability::Process, which issues no log barrier at all. Measured on this host with the harness's exact construction: 64 warm appends -> fsync delta 0; 64 new-stream appends -> fsync delta 0. There is no fsync signal to assert on in this mode, so option 1 is dead here. (Also bn-2di deleted the fjall name barrier entirely — a name persist is now a $registry batch riding the append's own commit group.)

Why registry records: since bn-2di, interning a name writes a RegistryEventV1 into the $registry log stream, one per stream name and one per event-type name, ever (REG4). That is exact and scheduling-independent. Measured: 64 new-stream commands -> 65 records (64 stream names + 1 'rel-touch' type); 256 warm appends to an interned stream -> 0 records. Asserted with assert_eq!, not an inequality — no coalescing ambiguity exists for record counts.

Plumbing: zero production changes. registry_records() reaches the engine via ProfilingBackend::inner() (new one-line accessor on the harness's own wrapper) -> FjallSnapshotBackend::inner() (already pub) -> LogEngine::read_stream/total_events (already pub). The probe bypasses the ProfilingBackend so it never lands in the histograms it is compared against.

Shared helpers: run_new_streams_seq and run_warm_one_stream now also return the $registry delta over their measured window; the ignored full matrix prints it as a 'registry name persists' row and its stale 'durability flush' wording is corrected.

Kept: the append_batch-observed and load_snapshot-called assertions.

Evidence:
- cargo nextest run -p social --test seed_profile: 10/10 pass in a loop (plus 1 more after rebase onto epoch c0f20093).
- cargo nextest run -p social (122 tests, parallel): 5/5 pass.
- cargo clippy -p social --tests: no new warnings.
- just fmt-check: clean.
